analysis.title: Global Markets Outlook 2027: Growing Pains
key_insights: GS baseline for 2027 is friendly (stable growth, declining inflation, peaking policy rates), but the market cycle is aging: real rates are higher, credit spreads wider and volatility rising under the surface. Risks are to the downside, and the broad asset picture is more two-sided, which argues for diversified and better-hedged portfolios.

The AI investment impulse (additional AI investment as a share of GDP) is forecast to peak in early 2027, with the peak in the investment share itself in 2028. The macro effect should be manageable, but markets face a bigger test because AI contributed more to earnings and market value growth than to GDP growth.

Companies levered to AI infrastructure have de-rated significantly since June, after being the biggest market beneficiaries in 1H 2026. Valuation excesses are less visible than in the late 1990s, so the debate is whether record profits are sustainable.

S&P 500 earnings growth is forecast to slow from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027. S&P 500 earnings are at a record share of GDP. GS says this slowdown should limit the de-rating but also implies less relief in core rates pricing.

GS expects the equity baton to pass from AI infrastructure to other areas: hyperscalers if monetization becomes visible, AI-productivity beneficiaries, and non-AI companies as capital crowding-out eases. The risk is that the transition is slow or that tighter financial and credit conditions feed back, turning a rotation into a larger aggregate shock. Risk to markets is judged higher than risk to the economy.

An oil spike from renewed escalation in the Iran war is one of the largest near-term risks. It would hurt equities, support the Dollar against European currencies and push rates up. Europe is vulnerable this winter because natural gas storage is low.

GS baseline is a gradual decline in energy prices even without full resolution of the conflict, since oil supply has largely been restored. Faster resolution in Iran or Ukraine is a key upside risk for broader markets, because lower energy prices would support both bonds and equities.

The Brent risk premium fell recently after peaking at the end of October. Energy's hedge value is higher when the premium is low. When the premium is very high, outright longs have been riskier than options, and oil is more exposed to downside tails on better news.

GS argues for higher bond allocations: running yield is good with a decent spread to cash, valuations are cheap, positioning is underweight, and there are paths to shallow rate relief. Central bank pricing in the US and UK is too hawkish relative to GS baseline. GS sees UST 10y yields at 4.6% by end-2027.

Bonds have been a poor hedge in 2026 under energy supply shocks and rate hikes, but are starting to hedge again as the shock shifts from energy to AI and demand stresses. Bunds rallied as French spreads widened, and USTs rallied when tech stocks fell. Equity-bond correlations have turned more negative.

GS pencils in about a 3% fall in the broad trade-weighted Dollar in 2027 as US inflation converges to target, energy prices fall and the Fed moves from hikes to cuts in late 2027 and early 2028. The Dollar's premium valuation has depended on equity inflows chasing US tech outperformance.

If US tech performance erodes meaningfully, GS expects Dollar underperformance rather than a safe-haven bid. The undervalued Yen is seen as the better hedge, helped by Japanese authorities focusing on limiting Yen depreciation. GS also sees scope for further gradual Yuan appreciation on a growing trade surplus and deep undervaluation.

Europe is pressured by the energy terms-of-trade shock, higher global yields and French sovereign stress. French fiscal issues are unlikely to be addressed until the Spring 2027 French election. Low carry and skewed risks keep downside optionality on EUR attractive near term, and EUR is a popular funding currency.

UK: Gilts have the highest beta to oil among developed markets, so they should gain most from falling energy prices. UK equities are defensive given low tech weight, though they have significant energy exposure. Sterling is the most overvalued G10 currency, and GS sees further gains as harder given its monetary policy forecasts are the most dovish relative to market pricing.

AI financing has pushed credit and equity issuance to cycle records. Issuance has been digestible but at discounted pricing, and AI-related credits have clearly underperformed in the last 6 months. GS expects further modest widening in index-level US credit spreads in 2027, with risks skewed toward wider and modest US HY underperformance (decompression).

Credit outlook splits by region and product: Europe offers more risk premium and room to tighten, while mortgages and structured credit offer refuge from heavy corporate supply. GS expects bifurcation between AI-related issuers and everything else, with episodic indigestion of jumbo AI debt deals. Hyperscaler free cash flow has deteriorated sharply.

EM has been resilient again in 2026, with EM equities on track for a double-digit year after 30% gains in 2025. Valuations are now less compelling: EM credit spreads are the tightest in years and local rate spreads are tight. The case rests on high diversified yields in EM fixed income (South Africa, Hungary, Colombia, India cited for improving fiscal stories) and a diversified earnings mix in EM equities, especially equal-weighted exposure. EM local assets offer upside convexity if core rates or the Dollar fall more than the baseline.

Tail hedges GS flags: lower rates in the US and Japan, or jointly lower rates and equities. Also USD/JPY downside, European gas futures and TTF call spreads, EUR funding, OTM equity puts, and longer-dated call options replacing equity holdings. Equity index volatility has risen a little, is unlikely to fall much, and has scope to rise if macro stresses broaden.

GS baseline forecasts positive 2027 returns for both equities and bonds. Real yields are historically high in absolute and relative terms. Later in 2027 the key risks increasingly favor bonds as central bank hike, energy spike and AI investment tailwind threats recede.

sector_views.rationale: Already de-rated since June. Investment impulse peaks early 2027, and profits at record share of GDP may not persist.
Gains may pass from AI infrastructure to hyperscalers if monetization paths become more visible.
Defensive with low tech weight and resilient, though with significant energy exposure.
Diversified earnings mix across North Asia tech, South Africa, LatAm and India. Equal-weighted exposure favored.
Baseline is muted returns on gradual price declines, but energy has high hedge value against escalation.

earnings_insights: GS forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth of 36% in 2026 slowing to 11% in 2027 (GS forecast).
S&P 500 total earnings are at a record share of GDP (Exhibit 2, 4-quarter moving average).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Slowing but still robust growth should limit the de-rating of AI-exposed areas and imply less relief in core rates pricing.
GS views yields as cheap at this level, supporting higher bond allocations.
Softer Dollar as inflation, energy prices and Fed hike pricing fade.

macro_indicators.reading: move from hikes to cuts as we head into late 2027 and early 2028
macro_indicators.interpretation: Policy rates peak lower than in 2023-2024 and reverse earlier. Market pricing is too hawkish.
Second-derivative turning point that ends the period of positive surprises and caps upside. The peak in the investment share itself is in 2028.

macro_indicators.reading: gradual decline in baseline, with risks skewed to the upside
macro_indicators.interpretation: Baseline assumes 2027 Gulf supply 1.1mb/d above 2025 average. Downside and upside cases are 2.5mb/d above and below.

trade_ideas.description: Position for lower rates in the US and Japan, or jointly lower rates and equities, as protection against deeper downside growth tails
trade_ideas.rationale: Growth risks skew down, and a growing number of risks would push both growth and rate expectations lower.
trade_ideas.risk: Oil spike or sticky core inflation would push rates higher.

trade_ideas.description: Long USD/JPY downside (short USD/JPY) as a hedge that performs when rates and equities fall together
trade_ideas.rationale: Yen is undervalued and typically sensitive to equities and rates falling together, and Japanese authorities want to limit Yen weakness.

trade_ideas.description: European gas futures and TTF call spreads as asymmetric protection against energy upside, plus EUR funding
trade_ideas.rationale: Low gas storage leaves Europe vulnerable to supply and weather risks this winter.

trade_ideas.description: Buy out-of-the-money equity puts, or replace equity holdings with longer-dated call options
trade_ideas.rationale: Protection is more valuable than usual as the cycle matures and volatility has scope to rise.

trade_ideas.description: Downside optionality on EUR (EUR funder trade)
trade_ideas.rationale: Skew of risks and low carry, with French fiscal concerns persisting until the Spring 2027 election.
Good running yield, cheap valuations, underweight positioning and paths to rate relief.
trade_ideas.risk: Energy shock extends, or inflation is stickier and the labour market stays resilient.

trade_ideas.description: Long UK Gilts, which have the highest beta to oil among DM bonds, for relief if energy pressures fall
trade_ideas.rationale: Falling oil would give the most relief to UK rates and the fiscal picture.

trade_ideas.description: Long EM local currency bonds and equal-weighted EM equities for diversified yield and earnings
trade_ideas.rationale: High diversified yields with improving fiscal stories, and upside convexity if core rates or the Dollar fall more than the baseline.
trade_ideas.risk: Valuations are less compelling after outperformance.

trade_ideas.rationale: Growing trade surplus and deep undervaluation that forward markets underestimate.

risk_factors: Escalation in the Iran war driving an oil spike, which could pressure equities and bonds together.
Peak in AI investment turning into a larger aggregate market shock if the baton does not pass smoothly or the market looks ahead to the 2028 peak in the investment share.
Tighter financial and credit conditions creating a feedback loop with AI-related drawdowns.
Sticky core inflation or a more resilient labour market keeping central banks hawkish.
Credit indigestion from jumbo AI debt financing and weaker borrowers in the left tail.
French fiscal stress ahead of the Spring 2027 election and a precarious European winter on low gas storage.
Erosion of US tech exceptionalism undermining the Dollar's premium valuation and global equity flows.
Cybersecurity fears and AI-related labour-shedding as growth-negative shocks.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 splits AI contribution to growth: US GDP 21%, US capex 62%, US earnings 62%, US market value (peak) 92%, US market value (YTD) 41%, per the plotted values in the text.
Exhibit 2 plots S&P 500 total earnings as a share of GDP (4-quarter moving average) from 1995 to present, at a record, with a dotted 1995-present linear trend.
Exhibit 7 plots 1-week and 1-month S&P 500/10Y US Treasury correlation from Dec-25 to Nov-26, with equity-bond correlations turning more negative as the shock shifts from energy to AI.
Exhibit 9 plots 10y bond total returns since January 1, 2026 against 2y1y sensitivity to oil, with UK gilts showing the highest beta to oil.
vol_and_positioning: Equity index volatility has risen a little but is unlikely to fall much and has scope to rise further if macro stresses broaden. The sharpest volatility so far is under the surface of major indices.
Deeper equity protection via OTM puts or replacing equity holdings with longer-dated call options is more valuable than usual as the cycle matures.
Bond positioning is underweight, and EUR is a popular funding currency for other crosses.
Downside optionality on EUR is attractive given skewed risks and low carry.
Equity-bond correlation has turned more negative as the market shifts from energy pressure to AI pressure (Exhibit 7), improving bond hedging value.
geopolitical: Iran war: risk of another escalation and new supply disruptions could spike oil. Oil supply has largely been restored despite limited refining capacity.
Faster resolution of Iran and Ukraine conflicts is a key upside risk for broader markets.
French election in Spring 2027 is the point by which French fiscal issues may be addressed, keeping EUR downside attractive until then.
Japanese policy authorities are focused on limiting Yen depreciation and encouraging inflows into Japanese assets.
China's growing trade surplus supports gradual Yuan appreciation, while domestic demand is very weak.
Europe faces a precarious winter with low natural gas storage.

tension_points.bull_case: AI investment and earnings growth stay firmly positive in 2027 (S&P 500 earnings +11%), and the baton passes to hyperscalers, AI users and non-AI companies as capital crowding-out eases.
tension_points.bear_case: The market looks ahead to the 2028 peak in the investment share, the rotation is slower than needed, or financial and credit conditions feed back into a larger aggregate shock.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A transition that does not take place quickly or smoothly, or feedback loops from financial and credit conditions accelerating faster than baseline.

tension_points.bull_case: Baseline has gradual decline in energy prices as supply is restored, and faster resolution in Iran or Ukraine would support both bonds and equities.
tension_points.bear_case: Escalation in the Iran war or new supply disruptions spikes oil, hurting equities, supporting the Dollar against European currencies and lifting rates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Broadening of the conflict and new supply disruptions.

tension_points.bull_case: Good running yield, cheap valuations, underweight positioning and a pivot from supply shocks to demand stresses make bonds a better hedge.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy shock extends further or inflation stays sticky while the labour market remains resilient, keeping central banks hawkish.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Extension of the energy shock or stickier inflation with a resilient labour market.
